title: Antony and Cleopatra
objective: After this level you can describe the alliance of Mark Antony and Cleopatra and why it alarmed Rome.
summary: Antony ruled the East and allied with Cleopatra, last of the Ptolemies. When he gave her Roman lands, Octavian called him a traitor.

cards.headline: A Roman general and an Egyptian queen formed a partnership Rome called treason.
The queen of Egypt
cards.body: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of Egypt’s Ptolemaic dynasty, a Greek-speaking family descended from a general of Alexander the Great. She had earlier been Julius Caesar’s ally and lover, and had a son, Caesarion, whom she said was Caesar’s.

cards.headline: Antony in the East
cards.body: After Philippi, Mark Antony took charge of Rome’s eastern provinces and allied with Cleopatra. He married Octavian’s sister Octavia in 40 BCE, but later left her for Cleopatra. In 34 BCE, in the Donations of Alexandria, he gave Roman lands in the East to Cleopatra and her children.

cards.fact: Octavian turned the romance into a weapon.
cards.context: He portrayed Antony as a traitor under the spell of a foreign queen, and opinion in Rome turned against Antony.

questions.prompt: From Level 41: after which battle did Antony take charge of the East?
questions.explanation: After Antony and Octavian beat Brutus and Cassius at Philippi, Antony took charge of the eastern provinces.
